summary: Inspect a licensed supplied adult dry-skull teaching mesh using curated cranial-fossa aperture labels and internal/external route anchors without detecting anatomy from holes.
objective: Inspect a licensed supplied adult dry-skull teaching mesh using curated cranial-fossa aperture labels and internal/external route anchors without detecting anatomy from holes.
example_prompts: Build dry-skull foramina exploded route atlas with explicit provenance, laterality, frame and unavailable-state checks.
negative_signals: infer missing clinical data from geometry
not_for: Diagnosis, treatment, procedure guidance or patient-specific inference.

entities.name: Source skull
entities.guidance: Preserve an unmodified, licensed mesh collection and record that OpenStax licenses its text/figures, not the chosen mesh.

entities.name: Paired apertures
entities.guidance: Curate side, fossa, internal/external anchors and passage label; camera never determines anatomical left/right.

entities.name: Exploded view
entities.guidance: Move bone parts by display matrices while route measurements remain in source coordinates.

state_contract.model: Each aperture record stores stable ID, anatomical side, fossa, source anchors, label confidence and provenance; missing anchors remain unavailable.
state_contract.authority: Supplied source records, identifiers, frames and curated labels own state. Blender/glTF geometry is display-only; Three.js owns validated runtime binding and exact reset.

invariants: Laterality survives camera orbit and mirrored layout.
Foramen lacerum is a dry-skull opening filled by cartilage in life, not a generic through-route.
Exploded matrices never alter source measurements.
motion_guidance: Exploded motion applies reversible display matrices to named bone nodes while source-space anchors and laterality stay fixed; Blender authors neutral parts/anchors, glTF transports their stable names, and Three.js owns the display transition and exact reset.
creative_affordances: Use restrained cutaways, translucent planes and non-color selection cues without implying clinical confidence.
known_limits: Documentary source review only; no dataset, patient record, simulation, specialist clinical validation or runtime was used.

claims.statement: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e describes cranial fossae and the locations or passage roles of major openings including optic canal, orbital fissure, foramina rotundum/ovale/spinosum, carotid canal, foramen lacerum, internal acoustic meatus, hypoglossal canal and jugular foramen; it notes foramen lacerum is filled with cartilage in life.
claims.scope: Section 7.2 adult dry-skull educational description; not a complete variant or transmitted-structure atlas.

source_refs.locator: Section 7.2, Figures 7.8 and 7.16, Cranial Fossae opening lists

object_craft.structure: Blender keeps the licensed source mesh unmodified, separates teaching-display bone parts non-destructively, and authors named aperture/route anchors in the declared source frame; glTF exports static parts, node names and neutral transforms.
object_craft.material: Matte bone, translucent fossa plates and glyph-coded routes; OpenStax content is not a geometry license.
object_craft.articulation: Three.js owns side-safe ID binding, source-to-display matrices, route lines, unavailable states and exact neutral reset; source measurements never read displaced mesh coordinates.

physical_contract.scope: Display of supplied educational or derived biomedical records; no tissue mechanics or diagnostic model.
checks: Reject ambiguous side, unit or frame.
